features.title: An answered question form stays closed while its reply waits for admission
features.summary: Answering a continued ask_user_question form queues a user-question-reply in the Inbox. The step boundary claims that reply, emptying the Inbox several awaits before the admitted user message settles the question, and the native client republished the form for that gap, so the panel closed, came back, then closed. The fork records each call this Client answered until the Host stops listing it and keeps that form out of the composer seat; the tool call row can still reveal it.
failureModes: A reply that never reaches admission keeps its card, so the tool call row can still reveal the form.
A projection with no value for the Session leaves the answered record in place instead of treating the call as settled.

verification.reason: src/native/index.ts is upstream revision 69f2241e of packages/client/ui-user-questions verbatim, whose browser-plugin.client.spec.ts covers both states (an answered form stays closed across the claimed-reply gap; a discarded reply stays revealable). The vendored components import browser-only native bundles this repository's Vitest cannot load; scripts/native-fork-diff.mjs proves every other vendored file equals the pinned tag.

features.title: Markdown questions with sandboxed HTML previews
features.summary: ask_user_question text and option descriptions render as markdown in the question form. The first paragraph is the heading (inline links, code and emphasis render in an ARIA heading; plain text keeps the native h2); the rest renders through the native MarkdownText (GFM tables, links, images, fenced code, math), through Chat's FencedMarkdown, so a fence a code-fence renderer claims (a ```mermaid diagram with @dshfiles/mermaid-diagrams) renders as it does in the transcript. A ```html preview fence renders through the QuestionHtmlPreview registry, which @dshfiles/html-render provides with its sandboxed card; a markdown option description renders under its option button so its links stay links. @dshfiles/tool-ask-user tells the model about it.
failureModes: Without @dshfiles/html-render the html preview fence shows as an html code block; the page never runs outside a sandbox.
A preview over 512 KB is refused in place with a recovery path (shrink it, or publish it with html_render).

The preview frame runs scripts without same-origin under a no-network Content-Security-Policy: external scripts, styles, fonts, images and fetch are blocked, and it cannot read DSH storage or the Host API.
Markdown images follow the chat transcript's policy: absolute local paths resolve through the file API and https images load directly; anything else renders as its alt text.
A plain ```html fence or an unclosed preview fence renders as code.

verification.testName: the first paragraph is the heading and the rest is the markdown body
an html preview fence becomes a preview between prose segments
a plain html fence is code, not a page
